title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: decode header according to the Bluetooth Core specification (v5.2), Vol 2 Part B Chapter 6.4
description:
According to the [LINKTYPE_BLUETOOTH_BREDR_BB Packet Structure](http://www.whiterocker.com/bt/LINKTYPE_BLUETOOTH_BREDR_BB.html) specification, the Bluetooth header should be formatted according to the Bluetooth specification Volume 2, Part B, Section 6.4. However, right now wireshark expects the header to be in a weird format (see this [Issue](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/17108)), specifically it expects the header fields to be MSB but the bits within each header field to be LSB. (Bluetooth standard is all LSB). Furthermore, it computes the HEC (header check, i.e. the header CRC) with 4 bits arbitrarily masked.

This patch decodes the header according to the spec. It still accepts the old format (if the broken HEC matches), and displays a warning.

I was wondering too what the original author used as capture mechanism. I unfortunately couldn't find this out, and the email address of the original author now bounces. I couldn't find a sample capture file either.
don't use the same display filter for all type ?
See answer below

I did not change that part. Changing it would break existing display filters.

Also, I think it makes sense like this. All of these hf_packet_header_type* are mutually exclusive. The Type field has partly the same, partly different meanings depending on context (logical transport it appears on). So these different hf_packet_header_type* are used to give the correct (according to context) string representation of the field encoding via different value_string tables.

Right now, for example, displaying all poll packets can be achieved with btbredr_rf.packet_header.type == 1. With your change, it would need seven terms.

The only thing that would get slightly simpler with your change is for example displaying only EV3 packets. This currently looks like btbredr_rf.payload_transport_rate.transport == 2 && btbredr_rf.packet_header.type >= 6 && btbredr_rf.packet_header.type <= 7, while in your case the transport check could be dropped.

commits_data.title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: No header for packets with inquiry access code
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: No header for packets with inquiry access code

Some "packets" have neither packet header nor payload. Unfortunately,
the BT BR/EDR pseudoheader has no flag whether there was a packet
header. Implement some heuristics to determine whether there was a
header. If the access code is one of the inquiry access code range,
there is usually no packet header unless it is an FHS packet.

commits_data.title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: Header decode improvements
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: Header decode improvements

According to Vol 2 Part B Chapter 6.5.1.4, FHS packets should always
employ a HEC UAP equal to DCI (== 0x00). This patch therefore checks
the HEC checksum for FHS packets even if the UAP is not valid in the
pseudoheader.

The reverse_bits implementation has been made slightly more efficient.
